title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck research note. It is page 3 of a Bourbaki congress report ('Tribu n° 65'). The report gives editorial instructions for redrafting a chapter draft titled 'Algèbres étales et la différente', intended for Commutative Algebra. It ended up in the correspondences / standard-conjectures folder, between pages of Grothendieck's proof that the Lefschetz-decomposition projections lie in the algebra A of correspondences. The content, in modern terms, is as follows.

(1) End of a local structure theorem for étale algebras. If B is étale over A at a prime q, there is an element x with B' = A[x] (presented as A[X]/(F)) such that F'(x) is invertible in the localization of B' at q∩B'. The map from that localization to B_q is bijective. So étale is locally 'standard étale'. The report asks for a generalization to B a localization of a finite A-algebra.

(2) If the localization of A at q∩A is normal and B is étale at q, then B_q is normal (ascent of normality along étale maps). Improvements depending on Zariski's Main Theorem are to be added between asterisks.

(3) n° 5, automorphism groups: a proposition on automorphisms of étale algebras, extended to the noetherian non-reduced case.

(4) n° 6, a criterion of non-ramification. For A local with maximal ideal m, fraction field K and KB = L, the following are equivalent:
- the discriminant criteria (i), (ii);
- (iii) B is finite over A and B/mB is étale over A/m;
- (iv) B is finite étale over A.
The referenced lemma, the existence of a primitive element of an étale algebra over a field, is proved by noting that P(x) = D(1, x, ..., x^{n-1}) (discriminant of the power basis) is a polynomial function of x. P is nonzero, as one sees after base change to the algebraic closure, so some x has P(x) ≠ 0.

(5) Globalization: B is finite étale over A iff each B_m is finite étale over A_m, iff B is finite over A and every fibre B/mB is étale.

(6) Proposed appendix: for a nilpotent ideal I of A, reduction mod I is an equivalence between finite étale A-algebras and finite étale A/I-algebras, with a pointer to SGA.

The page serves Bourbaki's (never completed) treatment of étale algebras within Commutative Algebra.
errors: The primitive-element argument (choose x with P(x) ≠ 0 from P ≠ 0) needs the ground ring/field to be infinite, or at least large enough; over a finite field a nonzero polynomial can vanish identically as a function. The finite case must be handled separately (e.g. by a cyclicity argument), and the report does not mention this.

The page is a Bourbaki editorial report, not a mathematical text by Grothendieck, and is unrelated to the surrounding pages on correspondences and Lefschetz projections. It is likely misfiled or archived alongside them.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine Bourbaki editorial report on a draft about étale algebras. All results are standard and appear in SGA 1 / EGA IV. Its only interest is historical: it documents Bourbaki's planned but unpublished étale-algebra chapter, and its presence in the Grothendieck correspondences folder.
transcription_corrections: Header 'Tribu n° 65' and the editorial style ('le texte', 'on le vide', 'Référer à Alg. IX') identify this as a Bourbaki report, not Grothendieck's handwritten notes; the machine transcription is otherwise essentially accurate.
'q' throughout is a fraktur \mathfrak{q} (prime ideal), and 'm' in 'B/mB' is \mathfrak{m}; both are correctly rendered.
